[#hash-password-hashing-compare]
.What each of "Password hashing" is
[cols="2,1,3,2,1,2",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Output | Security | Standard | Status | In the browser (WebCrypto)

| <<hash-argon2id,`argon2id`>>
| 16 to 2^32 - 1 bytes
| each guess costs its memory and passes, on a GPU too
| RFC 9106, one lane
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2d`>>
| 4 to 2^32 - 1 bytes
| the strongest against trade-offs, open to side channels on a shared machine
| RFC 9106, every parameter
| where no attacker shares the machine
| no

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2i`>>
| 4 to 2^32 - 1 bytes (16 or more on libsodium)
| each guess costs its memory and passes, but with few passes an attacker trades memory for time more cheaply than against Argon2id
| RFC 9106, every parameter
| legacy
| no

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2id`>>
| 4 to 2^32 - 1 bytes (16 or more on libsodium)
| each guess costs its memory and passes, on a GPU too
| RFC 9106, every parameter
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-scrypt,`scrypt`>>
| 1 to (2^32 - 1) times 32 bytes
| each guess costs 128 r N bytes of memory
| RFC 7914
| recommended
| no

| <<hash-bcrypt,`bcrypt`>>
| 60 characters: the version, the cost, the salt and the hash
| each guess costs 2^cost rounds of Blowfish's key schedule in 4 KiB of memory; it reads at most 72 bytes of a password
| Provos and Mazieres, A Future-Adaptable Password Scheme (USENIX 1999), as OpenBSD's bcrypt(3) writes it
| legacy
| no

| <<hash-bcrypt,`bcrypt_pbkdf`>>
| 1 to 1,024 bytes
| each round costs a bcrypt key schedule; its output blocks are interleaved, so that an attacker computes them all
| OpenBSD's bcrypt_pbkdf(3), as OpenSSH's private keys use it
| legacy
| no
|===

[#hash-password-hashing-choose]
.How to choose among "Password hashing"
[cols="2,2,2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Fastest natively | Smallest on Emscripten | Where it is used | Choose it when

| <<hash-argon2id,`argon2id`>>
| 38.3 ms (sodium)
| 39,690 bytes (sodium)
| link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP's first choice for password storage]; link:https://www.password-hashing.net/[the Password Hashing Competition's winner]; link:https://bitwarden.com/help/kdf-algorithms/[Bitwarden's vault key, as an option]
| Storing passwords and deriving keys from them.

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2d`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106[RFC 9106's variant where no attacker shares the machine, such as proof of work]
| Never for passwords; only where a format names Argon2d and no attacker shares the machine.

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2i`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://github.com/jedisct1/libsodium/blob/master/src/libsodium/include/sodium/crypto_pwhash_argon2i.h[libsodium's crypto_pwhash_argon2i, its password hash before Argon2id]; link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106#section-4[RFC 9106's variant for memory access independent of the secret, which it recommends only through Argon2id]
| Only to check tags a system already stored with Argon2i; Argon2id for anything new.

| <<hash-argon2-family,`kdfs::argon2id`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9106#section-4[RFC 9106's first recommendation for password hashing]; link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP's first choice for password storage]
| Storing passwords and deriving keys from them where a parameter beyond the function argon2id's is needed (lanes, a pepper, associated data); argon2id otherwise.

| <<hash-scrypt,`scrypt`>>
| 19.1 ms (sodium)
| 29,540 bytes (sodium)
| link:https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/data-structures-and-encoding/web3-secret-storage/[Ethereum's keystore files (Web3 Secret Storage)]; link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP: N 2^17, r 8, p 1 when Argon2id is not available]
| When a format demands scrypt; otherwise Argon2id.

| <<hash-bcrypt,`bcrypt`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://man.openbsd.org/bcrypt.3[OpenBSD's password hashes, and those of the many systems that store its strings]; link:https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html[OWASP: for legacy systems where Argon2id and scrypt are not available, a cost of 10 or more]
| To check or make the bcrypt strings a system already stores; Argon2id for a new design.

| <<hash-bcrypt,`bcrypt_pbkdf`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/master/PROTOCOL.key[OpenSSH's private key files, their kdfname bcrypt]; link:https://man.openbsd.org/bcrypt_pbkdf.3[OpenBSD's bcrypt_pbkdf(3)]
| To read or write OpenSSH's encrypted private keys; Argon2id for a new design.
|===

The measured columns are doc/measurements.json's, a reference measured on 2026-11-16 on Apple M5 Max that decides nothing: the native throughput over 1 MiB, or the time of one derivation over `hmac_sha2_256`, of the fastest backend, and the smallest Emscripten program that calls the function; <<hash-measurements>> has every backend on every target.
